text:
sara_support: Hey team, ticket escalated — customer reports duplicate POSTs and duplicate billing when our TS SDK retries. They're on Node 18.16 + undici and using AbortController to cancel requests on client timeout. They say duplicates appear intermittently under high latency. Attached minimal repro below.

devon_engineer: Thanks — can you paste the repro and SDK version? Also whether they enabled `retry` option in our SDK or set custom backoff.

sara_support: SDK v1.3.0, default retry policy (3 attempts), they pass a shared AbortController to downstream fetch calls. Repro snippet from customer:

```
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 400); // client-side timeout
await redwoodClient.post('/responses', { body }, { signal: ac.signal });
```

They also have a global fetch wrapper that reuses agent: `new UndiciAgent({ keepAlive: true })` and pass it to all requests.

michael_ops: Quick theory: undici + shared AbortController + our retry wrapper can cause the first attempt to be aborted locally but the runtime still issues subsequent retries with a stale/ignored signal or race. In some Node/undici versions aborting can leave the stream in weird state causing server to receive partial/duplicate POSTs.

devon_engineer: Can we get the raw server logs showing duplicate request IDs or same payload? Also need the exact `undici` version. Undici had a fix around 5.22 for signal handoff timing.

sara_support: Customer sent headers from duplicate entries — same idempotency key absent. They say they don't set Idempotency-Key header. Logs show two full POSTs within ~200ms. undici@5.21.0.

devon_engineer: Repro steps I recommend for us to try locally:
1) run Node 18.16 with undici@5.21.0
2) small express endpoint that logs body and returns 200 after 250ms
3) client uses our SDK retry config and shared AbortController with client timeout ~400ms

If we reproduce, test two mitigations: a) ensure per-request new AbortController for each retry OR b) disable connection keepAlive / use agent per request to see if connection reuse is part of it.

michael_ops: Also try setting an `Idempotency-Key` in client as a band-aid for the customer. But need to confirm root cause. Might be our retry logic starting a retry even after abort event if signal handling order races with backoff timer.

devon_engineer: I tried a quick local repro. Confirmed duplicate bodies with undici@5.21.0 when reusing the same AbortController across retries. With undici@5.23.0 the duplicate goes away.

Here is a minimal failing client pattern I used:
```
// failing pattern
const signal = new AbortController();
client.request({ path: '/slow', method: 'POST', body, signal: signal.signal, retry: { retries: 2, backoff: 50 } });
setTimeout(() => signal.abort(), 300);
```

And the working patterns:
- create a fresh AbortController for each attempt (or do not pass signal to the retry layer), OR
- upgrade undici to >=5.23.0 where signal handoff bug fixed, OR
- set Idempotency-Key on POSTs.

sara_support: Customer is on a locked runtime and cannot upgrade undici easily. They asked for a quick SDK-side mitigation.

devon_engineer: We can implement a guard in SDK retry wrapper: if the user-provided signal is aborted, do not start retries. Also ensure we clone/ignore the original signal for subsequent attempts and create a new internal AbortController for each try. Quick patch idea:

```
// pseudo
if (userSignal?.aborted) throw new AbortError();
for (attempt...) {
  const attemptSignal = new AbortController();
  // if user aborts, propagate
  userSignal?.addEventListener('abort', () => attemptSignal.abort());
  await fetch(..., { signal: attemptSignal.signal });
}
```

michael_ops: That sounds safe. It avoids reusing the same signal object across retries which seems to trigger undici edge-case. Also log a metric when we skip retries due to aborted signal so customers see behavior.

sara_support: I'll propose that workaround to the customer: add Idempotency-Key or we can release small patch to SDK to use per-attempt signals and short-circuit retries if user signal aborted. Would you prefer a hotfix branch?

devon_engineer: Yes, open a release branch `fix/retries-signal-handling` and include tests against undici@5.21.0 and 5.23.0. Add integration test that simulates slow server and client abort to assert only single POST is received.

deploy-bot: Created issue #4387 and branch fix/retries-signal-handling. CI will run matrix: node 18/20, undici 5.21/5.23.

sara_support: Thanks — passing mitigation suggestions to the customer (Idempotency-Key + avoid shared AbortController) and will update when patch/rollout scheduled. :thumbsup:
